originalPassage: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressing to your ear.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어의 핵은 단수 명사인 'The fast pace'이므로 단수 동사 has를 쓴 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 동사 'know'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로, 뒤에 완전한 절(multitasking doesn't save any time)이 이어지므로 that을 쓴 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 전치사 'to'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 동시에 절 안에서 동사 'doing'의 목적어 역할을 해야 하므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what을 쓴 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 동사 'accomplish'를 수식하여 '더 잘 완수하다'라는 의미를 나타내므로, 부사 'well'의 비교급인 better를 쓴 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 밑줄 친 (D)가 포함된 부분은 ‘~한 채로, ~한 상태에서’의 의미를 나타내는 「with + 명사(구) + 분사」 구문입니다. 이 구문에서 명사(구)와 분사의 관계가 능동인지 수동인지를 파악해야 합니다. 문맥상 명사 'your phone'이 귀에 '눌리는' 것이므로, 둘의 관계는 수동입니다. 따라서 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 pressing을 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 pressed로 고쳐야 어법상 올바른 표현이 됩니다. 학생들이 종종 with 구문에서 분사의 형태를 혼동하지만, 분사의 의미상 주어인 명사와의 관계를 따져보면 쉽게 구분할 수 있습니다.
keyPoints: (D) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — with 분사구문의 의미상 주어와의 관계 파악
(A) 주어-동사 수일치 — 수식어구를 제외한 주어의 핵 찾기
(C) 관계대명사 what vs 접속사 that — 이어지는 절의 완전성 여부로 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle __(A) has__ us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know __(B) that__ multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(C) what__ you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone __(D) pressing__ to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task __(E) better__, and probably faster.
